themes.name: Philosophy Over Tactics
themes.summary: The course argues that sustainable investing requires a coherent worldview about prices, behavior, and edge, not a pile of disconnected screens and tricks.

subthemes.name: A strategy is not a philosophy
subthemes.summary: Buying low PE stocks, trading charts, or following insiders are not philosophies by themselves; they need a deeper explanation for why they should work.

subthemes.name: Behavior sits underneath every investing style
subthemes.summary: Every philosophy makes an implicit claim about how investors think, misreact, herd, panic, or miss information.

subthemes.name: Valuation is the common language across styles
subthemes.summary: Even investors who disagree about what matters still need a way to connect expected cash flows, narratives, and prices.

themes.name: Risk, Return, and Friction
themes.summary: Risk is treated as inseparable from opportunity, but realized returns are also shaped by costs, taxes, and the actual path an investor must survive.

subthemes.name: Risk is danger plus opportunity
subthemes.summary: The course rejects the idea that risk is only a negative and insists that upside and downside are linked in investing.

subthemes.name: Different assets hide different risks
subthemes.summary: Bond risk, equity risk, price risk, and cash-flow risk are not interchangeable, and investors often measure the wrong thing.

subthemes.name: Implementation can destroy a good idea
subthemes.summary: High turnover, taxes, and trading friction mean that a theoretical edge may not survive real-world execution.

themes.name: Market Mistakes and Behavioral Edge
themes.summary: A large part of the course asks when markets are efficient, when they are slow, and when human behavior creates repeatable pricing errors.

subthemes.name: Efficiency is not all-or-nothing
subthemes.summary: Markets can be fast in some places, slow in others, and different across asset classes, information types, and investor populations.

subthemes.name: Patterns attract believers because they promise control
subthemes.summary: Momentum, calendar effects, and charting appeal to investors partly because they turn noisy markets into readable stories.

subthemes.name: Information does not become price cleanly
subthemes.summary: News passes through rumors, processing delays, different interpretations, and incentive conflicts before it becomes market price.

themes.name: Value Versus Growth Is Really About Where Value Lives
themes.summary: The course reframes the classic value-growth split as a disagreement about whether the best bargains live in existing assets or future growth assets.

subthemes.name: Value investing privileges assets in place
subthemes.summary: Value investors prefer businesses whose worth can be tied more directly to what already exists and can be analyzed with less speculation.

subthemes.name: Growth investing privileges underappreciated optionality
subthemes.summary: Growth investors are making a claim that the market is underestimating future expansion, reinvestment quality, or strategic upside.

subthemes.name: Activism appears on both sides
subthemes.summary: Both value and growth can become interventionist when investors stop waiting for recognition and start trying to change outcomes.

themes.name: The Industrial Problem of Edge
themes.summary: Many philosophies sound attractive in isolation, but the course repeatedly asks whether they still work once many people know about them, compete for them, and commercialize them.

subthemes.name: Public strategies decay when they become crowded
subthemes.summary: Simple screens, public signals, and copied rules lose power as they become easier to identify, package, and arbitrage away.

subthemes.name: True arbitrage is scarce and temporary
subthemes.summary: Pure arbitrage is rare precisely because obvious riskless profits attract capital and disappear quickly.

subthemes.name: Many branded edges are really speculative bets
subthemes.summary: The course warns that the language of arbitrage or skill is often used to market trades that still carry meaningful risk.

themes.name: The Allure of Control Versus the Case for Humility
themes.summary: Investors are drawn to timing, stock-picking, and active repositioning because these activities offer a feeling of agency, but the course keeps returning to how hard it is to earn that confidence.

subthemes.name: Market timing is the ultimate control fantasy
subthemes.summary: Timing promises that investors can improve outcomes not just by choosing assets well, but by getting in and out at the right moments.

subthemes.name: Being right is not enough; you must be right on schedule
subthemes.summary: Timing strategies fail because they require correct judgment, correct sequencing, and behavioral stamina at the same time.

subthemes.name: Passive investing is a philosophy of disciplined humility
subthemes.summary: The passive case is not laziness; it is a sober response to the empirical weakness and inconsistency of active outperformance.

themes.name: Investing Is Also Cultural, Social, and Institutional
themes.summary: Several parts of the course show that assets gain traction not only from cash flows, but from identity, trust, status, ideology, and the institutions investors either rely on or reject.

subthemes.name: Authority and influence shape information markets
subthemes.summary: Insiders, analysts, and portfolio managers matter not just because they may know more, but because the market assigns them social authority.

subthemes.name: Alternative assets often sell identity as much as return
subthemes.summary: Collectibles, private assets, and certain alternatives gain appeal from exclusivity, taste, signaling, and stories of uniqueness.

subthemes.name: Bitcoin emerges from distrust in institutions
subthemes.summary: Crypto is framed as an asset class born from skepticism toward governments, banks, and centralized verification systems.

themes.name: Portfolio Fit Matters More Than Universal Recipes
themes.summary: The course ends by suggesting that the right philosophy depends on temperament, informational advantage, tax position, time horizon, and willingness to live with the consequences.

subthemes.name: A philosophy must match the investor, not just the spreadsheet
subthemes.summary: A strategy can be analytically sound and still fail if the investor cannot hold it through drawdowns, complexity, or social pressure.

subthemes.name: Asset choice is inseparable from implementation constraints
subthemes.summary: Taxes, liquidity, time horizon, and operational simplicity strongly influence what should actually go into a portfolio.

subthemes.name: The end goal is consistency, not style collecting
subthemes.summary: The final synthesis is not to know every philosophy, but to choose one or a few that can be practiced coherently over time.
